summary: Specializing in sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, Michael Stanley-Baker earned an MA at Indiana University under Stephen R. Bokenkamp (attested 2006). His posts include appointments at NTU, Leipzig University, MPIWG, and the University of Pittsburgh.
Michael Torsten Much is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991). He has held a fellowship at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847) under Niels Ludvig Westergaard. He served at Copenhagen as 副司書 (1861) and Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Harvard (BA 1960–1964, MA 1968–1971, PhD 1971–1974) and the University of Pennsylvania. He became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania around 1976.

Michael Weiers was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies who completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965). He served as professor at Bonn (1972–2003) and honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University (~1996).

Michael Wenger is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at The New School and studied under Sojun Mel Weitsman. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1984–2012) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

Michael Willis is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Victoria and completed his doctorate at the University of Chicago (1988). He worked as a curator of South Asian Collections at the British Museum (1994–2014).

Michael Witzel is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Thieme, Hoffmann, Narten, Schmidt, Pandit, and Kuiper. He headed the Nepal Research Centre (1972–1978) and held Sanskrit chairs at Leiden (1978–1986) and Harvard (appointed 1986).

Michael Zimmermann works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, whom he later succeeded in 2007, and held posts at the Nepal Research Centre and Stanford University.

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who completed his Promotion at the University of Rostock (1968–1973). He held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).
Michaela Haas is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger. She also studied under Jigme Namgyel and Rechungpa.

Michaela Mross works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and earned her PhD from the University of Munich (2014), later holding positions at UC Berkeley and Stanford University (attested 2017).

Michel Bitbol is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Paris Diderot University (completed 1985) and under Pierre Mills. He held positions at CNRS (~1990), IHPST (~1990–2009), and École Normale Supérieure (~2010).

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, under Bopp, and under Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at the Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at the EPHE (~1868–1882).

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his studies and doctoral thesis at the University of South Africa (~1991–1999), where he also held an academic post beginning in 1990.

Michel Hulin was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1956) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1968–1977) under Olivier Lacombe. He held a post at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.
Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was an art historian and Indologist who studied under Jean Boisselier in 1988. He served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from approximately 1989 to 2008.

Michel Lejeune was a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) under Antoine Meillet. He held academic posts at the University of Poitiers (~1933–1937), the University of Paris (~1947–1951), and the EPHE (~1951–1977).

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who completed his PhD at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Michel Soymié was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO (~1948–1952). He served at CNRS (1951–1956), EFEO (~1952–1966), and held the Chair of History and Philosophy of Mediaeval China at EPHE (~1966–1992).
